title: Certificates: openssl to look inside
summary: Read a certificate, ask a server, check a chain and a key, and read the errors curl gives.

text: openssl x509 reads a certificate file. -noout skips the base64 block, and you name the fields you want.
- -text prints everything: useful once, a lot to read.
- A Mac's openssl is LibreSSL, without -ext: use -text and read under Subject Alternative Name (or brew install openssl@3).
s_client connects like a browser and shows what the server sends.
- -servername sends the name you want (SNI): a server with many sites picks its certificate by it.
- The connection opens even when the check fails: read the Verify return code line.
- -showcerts prints each certificate sent. LibreSSL (Mac) has no -verify_hostname.
openssl verify follows the signatures, with no network at all.
- -CAfile is what you trust. -untrusted gives the intermediates to link with, and trusts nothing by itself.
- fullchain.pem is what a server should send: its own certificate first, then the intermediates in order.

scheme: same lines: this key goes with this certificate
text: A server refuses to start when its key doesn't go with its certificate. Compare the public halves:
- the certificate holds the public key;
- the private key file holds both halves, and -pubout prints the public one.

scheme: unable to get local issuer        chain, or CA
text: Each certificate error says which part failed. Fix that part.
- unable to get local issuer: the server doesn't send its intermediates, or you don't trust its CA. For a private CA: curl --cacert ca.pem.
- ✘ curl -k (--insecure) hides every one of these errors, an attacker's certificate included.
